notes:
CIRCUIT: 24V DC source -> two parallel two-element blocks in series, with a 5A current source and a 50mH inductor shunting to a common ground rail. 8 components, 4 nets, 15 terminals. Left block: 100KOhm resistor (top branch, y~345) in parallel with a 25mH inductor (bottom branch, y~455), tied together by vertical bars at x~265 and x~453. Right block: 2pF capacitor (top, y~348) in parallel with a 10MOhm resistor (bottom, y~455), tied by vertical bars at x~568 and x~751.

NET MAP:
 n3 = the 24V source's top terminal (4.1) -> up to (192,400) -> right to the left bar of the left block at (265,421) [S10 T-junction] -> that bar feeds the 100K left lead (1.0) at its top and the 25mH left lead (3.0) at its bottom. 3 terminals.
 n1 = the right bar of the left block at x~453 (100K right 1.1, 25mH right 3.1) -> the y~400 wire running right, T-ing down at (510,404) [S7] into the 5A source top lead (6.0), then continuing to the left bar of the right block at (568,402) [S8], which feeds the 2pF left plate (0.0) and the 10M left lead (2.0). 5 terminals.
 n2 = the right bar of the right block at x~751 (2pF right 0.1, 10M right 2.1) -> the wire right at (751,400) [S6 T] to x~820 and down into the 50mH top lead (5.0). 3 terminals.
 0 = the bottom rail y~655 from the 24V source's bottom lead (4.0) at x~192 rightwards to x~820 and up into the 50mH bottom lead (5.1), with the 5A source's bottom lead (6.1) and the GND symbol's stub (7.0) both meeting it at (530,660) [S32]. 4 terminals.

JUDGEMENT CALLS: none needed - this sheet contains no wire crossings at all. Every intersection is an unambiguous T where a lead or a rail terminates on a through-wire.
 * S6 (751,400) - T: the right bar of the right block meets the wire heading to the 50mH. Inspected at 5x: the horizontal stub starts exactly on the vertical, no hop, no pass-through. JUNCTION.
 * S7 (510,404) - T: the y~400 rail runs straight through while a stub drops to the 5A source. JUNCTION (a crossing reading is impossible here - the downward stub is the only thing at that position, there is no opposite branch, and it would leave the 5A source top lead on a one-terminal net).
 * S8 (568,402) - T: the left bar of the right block meets the y~400 rail arriving from the left. JUNCTION.
 * S9 (453,404) - T: the right bar of the left block meets the y~400 rail leaving to the right; a small solder thickening is visible (dot=1.8). JUNCTION.
 * S10 (265,421) - T: the wire up from the 24V source meets the left bar of the left block mid-height. JUNCTION.
 * S32 (530,660) - 4-way T on the ground rail: rail left, rail right, the 5A source's bottom lead coming down, and the GND symbol's stub going down. Solder thickening present (dot=2.2). JUNCTION - all four are one node; reading it as a crossing would strand the GND stub with the source lead and split the bottom rail, leaving the 24V return path open.

OTHER CHECKS:
 * All 8 classes confirmed against the drawn symbols: 2 resistors (zig-zag), 2 inductors (coils), 1 capacitor (parallel plates), 1 V-DC (circled +/-), 1 I-DC (circled arrow), 1 GND (3 decreasing bars). No class changes.

 * The three 'unused port candidate' warnings (resistor #1 at (305,314), resistor #2 at (624,477), inductor #3 at (347,475)) are all strokes of the handwritten value labels '100 KOhm', '10 MOhm' and '25 mH' brushing the annotated boxes, not leads. Confirmed at 5x.
 * Nothing left unresolved.
